title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for parallel multi-tool calls and result injection/retries
author: Aditi Rao
release_notes: Improvements to tool-calling execution ergonomics: safer parallel tool invocation and deterministic result injection with retry semantics.
New API knobs for multi-tool parallelism and retry backoff; no breaking changes to OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
Behavioral changes: improved stability for streaming responses when tools are called in parallel; opt-in rollout.
description: Motivation: customers running multi-tool workflows (e.g., search + enrichment + external API calls) were seeing brittle behaviour in the face of transient tool failures and non-deterministic result injection order. This caused streaming glitches and application-level regressions. This PR improves execution ergonomics for multi-tool calls by: 1) introducing a deterministic result injection layer that preserves tool ordering where required; 2) enabling parallel tool execution with configurable concurrency and per-tool retry semantics; 3) making streaming/stage boundaries robust to delayed tool responses and partial failures. Summary of changes: - API: added optional parameters to the OpenAI-compat tool_call payload: "parallelism_hint", "inject_order": ("preserve"|"by_completion"), and "retry_policy" (backoff_ms, max_retries). These fields are opt-in and backward compatible. - Runtime: implemented a ParallelInvocationManager that schedules tool tasks with a priority queue, per-tool timeouts, and coordinated result injection into the response stream. The manager supports two injection strategies: preserve (in request-declared order) and by_completion (inject as results arrive). - Retries: added configurable per-tool exponential backoff with jitter and a lightweight circuit-breaker to avoid cascading failures. - Streaming: improved stream checkpointing so partially-injected transcripts remain valid and downstream clients can resume after transient failures. - Compatibility: OpenAI-compat layer now maps the new fields when present; absent fields retain legacy behaviour. - Tests & CI: added unit/integration tests covering common failure modes, flake-resistant timing tests, and an end-to-end scenario with mock external tools. Design notes and tradeoffs: - We intentionally keep the default behaviour identical to current production (serial injection, no retries) to avoid surprising existing customers. New opt-in fields allow progressive rollout. - Deterministic (preserve) injection requires buffering of results until earlier tools complete; to bound memory we keep a configurable buffer cap and degrade to by_completion if capacity exceeded (logged as a metric). - Retries are limited per-tool; long-running tools still respect overall request-level timeout. - We prioritized simplicity in the OpenAI-compat surface (few, well-named fields) and delegated policy complexity to server-side configs. Migration/Rollout: - Feature flagged behind rollout feature "tool-calling-ergonomics". - Canary rollout to 10% of traffic for 72 hours, monitor tool latency/error metrics and stream error rates. - Docs PR (redwood-docs) will be linked with examples and migration guidance. Related: referenced ENG-3210 (multi-tool UX) and ENG-3245 (streaming stability investigations). See also prior PRs: pr-54823 and pr-53789 (historical context).

review_conversation: Evan: Please clarify memory bounds when using 'preserve' injection. Aditi: Added buffer cap and metrics; documented fallback to by_completion when cap exceeded. Mariana: Are retries safe for idempotent vs non-idempotent tools? Suggest adding opt-in 'idempotent' flag on tool definitions. Aditi: Agreed and added an optional 'tool_definition.idempotent' check and a server-side guard that refuses auto-retries for non-idempotent tools unless explicitly marked. Jonah: CI timing tests flaked locally, added deterministic timing helpers and increased tolerance. Final: all reviewers approved, small follow-up requested to add docs examples for JS and Python SDKs.
